title: Product Thinking & Problem Framing
description: Turn vague ideas into user-centered problems, outcomes, constraints, and scope before asking an agent to build.

lessons.title: Start from the user problem
lessons.principle: Features are valuable only when they improve a real user task or outcome.
lessons.practice: Write the affected user, current pain, desired outcome, and evidence before discussing implementation.

lessons.title: Define the job to be done
lessons.principle: A job describes the progress a user is trying to make, independent of a specific UI.
lessons.practice: Frame requests around the task and context so the agent can consider better solution shapes.

lessons.title: Distinguish wants from requirements
lessons.principle: Stakeholder suggestions often mix goals with premature implementation choices.
lessons.practice: Separate mandatory outcomes and constraints from negotiable design ideas.

lessons.title: Define measurable success
lessons.principle: Without success criteria, an agent can optimize the wrong behavior.
lessons.practice: Specify metrics or observable outcomes such as completion rate, latency, accuracy, or reduced steps.

lessons.title: Map the primary user journey
lessons.principle: A feature is a sequence of states and decisions, not a single screen.
lessons.practice: Describe entry, happy path, alternatives, errors, recovery, and completion.

lessons.title: Identify actors and permissions
lessons.principle: Different users may see or change different data.
lessons.practice: List roles, ownership rules, and prohibited actions before building interfaces or APIs.

lessons.title: Clarify scope boundaries
lessons.principle: Vague scope invites unrelated refactors and feature creep.
lessons.practice: State in-scope behavior, explicit non-goals, and systems that must remain unchanged.

lessons.title: Capture constraints early
lessons.principle: Technical, legal, accessibility, budget, and schedule constraints shape viable solutions.
lessons.practice: Place hard constraints in the task brief so the agent cannot optimize around an impossible assumption.

lessons.title: Define data inputs and outputs
lessons.principle: Ambiguous data contracts lead to fragile interfaces.
lessons.practice: List required inputs, validation rules, outputs, side effects, and persistence expectations.

lessons.title: Design empty states
lessons.principle: Real products often start with no data.
lessons.practice: Specify what users see and can do before any content, configuration, or history exists.

lessons.title: Design loading states
lessons.principle: Asynchronous operations create visible intermediate states.
lessons.practice: Define progress, disabled actions, cancellation, and timeout behavior where relevant.

lessons.title: Design error and recovery states
lessons.principle: Failure is part of the user journey.
lessons.practice: Specify actionable messages, retry behavior, rollback, and what state must be preserved after failure.

lessons.title: Consider edge cases before code
lessons.principle: Boundary conditions discovered late often require structural rewrites.
lessons.practice: Enumerate unusual sizes, missing data, duplicate actions, concurrency, offline use, and permission changes.

lessons.title: Prioritize the smallest useful slice
lessons.principle: The first implementation should prove value without committing to unnecessary complexity.
lessons.practice: Choose a vertical slice that reaches a real user outcome end-to-end.

lessons.title: Avoid solution lock-in
lessons.principle: Early implementation choices can hide better approaches.
lessons.practice: Ask for two or three solution options with tradeoffs before committing on consequential architecture.

lessons.title: Use examples and counterexamples
lessons.principle: Concrete examples expose ambiguity faster than abstract prose.
lessons.practice: Provide representative valid cases, invalid cases, and tricky cases for important rules.

lessons.title: Model irreversible actions explicitly
lessons.principle: Deletion, billing, publication, and destructive migrations require extra safeguards.
lessons.practice: Require confirmations, permissions, auditability, and recovery plans for high-impact actions.

lessons.title: Define compatibility expectations
lessons.principle: New features may need to preserve old URLs, data, APIs, or behavior.
lessons.practice: State backward-compatibility constraints and migration windows explicitly.

lessons.title: Document unresolved questions
lessons.principle: Unknowns should be visible instead of silently guessed.
lessons.practice: Maintain an open-questions section and resolve blockers before irreversible implementation.

lessons.title: Write a decision-ready brief
lessons.principle: A good brief lets an implementer begin without repeatedly rediscovering intent.
lessons.practice: Summarize problem, users, scope, constraints, success, acceptance criteria, risks, and open questions.

codeExamples.snippet:
User: project owner
Problem: cannot recover from failed publish
Outcome: safe retry without duplicate side effects
Non-goal: redesign the editor

Success criteria:
- task completes in <= 3 steps
- errors preserve user input
- unauthorized users cannot perform the action
